item.title: The 3-2-1 Code Challenge
item.description:
Idea

A daily checklist with the goal of honing my tech skills and finding me a job in the area. The idea came about after I was looking for ways to be more productive (and get a job faster!)

Execution

Simple checklist, cannot get it wrong.

  • ✅ 3 programming exercises from Leetcode
  • ✅ 2 job applications
  • ✅ 1 blog post

Then, I will update this post weekly with the list and some stats. Hope it works!

item.title: Day #2 - Backend, fullstack or QA?
item.description:
Challenges

  • 283. Move Zeroes
  • 392. Is Subsequence
  • 11. Container With Most Water
Two pointers are very against my nature. I see the answer visible in my face, but I have a hard time translating it to numbers and code.

What helped with the subsequence question was figuring out there was an easy way to “lock in” with the j-pointer to make all the verifications before moving on the next iteration. That thinking did not work well with the container problem. I will revisit it tomorrow.

item.title: Day #1 - Leetcode and QA
item.description:
Challenges

  • 345. Reverse Vowels of a String
  • 151. Reverse Words in a String
  • 283. Move Zeroes

I will have to revisit moving zeroes to make sure it stick, it is not very intuitive despite sounding like such a simple thing to do.

Roles

Today I had a Python Developer Interview and I applied for a QA Tester interview.

item.title: How to Create a Hugo Blog Using GitHub
item.description:
I am a professional developer, but I believe you do not need to be one to build a blog with some code. There are many tools out there that (usually with a fee) allow us to create websites without programming, and it is okay to use them.

However, if you, like me, just want a simple blog that you’d like to have control over, likes to code you can go with this approach.
